faqs.question: Does Epson make drivers for Linux?
faqs.answer:
Linux drivers are available for some products. Visit the links below to see the drivers available for your product, as well as information about using an Epson product with Linux.
Note:
Epson does not provide support for Linux drivers.
Linux drivers for Epson products
Linux FAQs for Epson products
(only available in English)
Linux manuals for Epson products
(only available in English)

faqs.question: When I try to print to my product in Windows 7, printing is slow or my product stops printing. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Try the following:
Select a lower quality setting in the printer software.
Make sure your system meets the minimum system requirements for your printer.
Close the
Devices and Printers
window before you print.
Clear space on your hard drive or run a defragmentation utility.
Close programs that you're not using.
Increase your system's memory.

faqs.question: Can the Epson ink cartridges be refilled or can I use third-party ink cartridges without voiding the warranty?
faqs.answer:
Epson does not recommend refilling or using other brands of ink cartridges.  Epson uses a permanent Micro Piezo print head that has allowed Epson to lead the industry in delivering consistent photo image quality by using variable-sized droplets.  Micro Piezo print head can also use a wider variety of inks, which has allowed Epson to introduce such ink breakthroughs as DURABrite® and Epson UltraChrome® inks that offer greatly improved humidity resistance, smudge resistance, and fade resistance.
Using refilled ink cartridges will not void the product's original warranty; however, if these products cause a failure, the repair of that failure will not be covered under warranty.

faqs.question: I am unable to connect my product to a wireless network. What should I do?
faqs.answer: The printer does not come with built-in wireless features and does not support a wireless (or Ethernet) connection to a network router. Only a direct wired connection to the computer is supported.

faqs.question: I see the message Cannot connect to Internet in Windows 8.1 after I select Driver Update in my product software. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
The
Driver Update
option does not work in Windows 8.1. All other driver options will work correctly.

faqs.question: I brought my product with me to a different country and can't find ink for it. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Some Epson printers and ink cartridges are specific to a regional market and not sold worldwide, although the same printers are sold in the U.S. and Canada. If you have a printer sold in the U.S. or Canada, you may not be able to easily get ink cartridges for it in foreign markets.
Unfortunately, because of customs and tax regulations, the Epson E-Stores in the U.S. and Canada are unable to ship to addresses outside the U.S. and Canada.

faqs.question: Does Epson have a program where I can donate my working electronic equipment?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Epson America, Inc. and
Digitunity
have joined together with the goal of helping those who are facing economic challenges or have a disability to gain access to today's technology. With your donation, you not only help the environment, but you also help change the lives of those who need these products the most.

faqs.question: My product makes noise after I turn it on or after it has been sitting for a while. What should I do?
faqs.answer: This is normal. It is performing routine maintenance.

faqs.question: I can't find some of my printer's settings in macOS 12 or later. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Make sure you're using the Epson driver for your printer. See our
Adding a Printer in macOS 12 or Later

faqs.question: How can I print directly from an external drive or a memory drive with my product?
faqs.answer:
If you saved your photos to a CD, flash memory (thumb) drive, or Zip disk, you can connect the drive to the back of PictureMate and print just like you do when you insert a memory card. For more information, see
Printing From an External Drive
.

faqs.question: Why does it take so long to scroll through my pictures on my product's display?
faqs.answer: The file size of the pictures determines the viewing speed. Scrolling takes longer when you are viewing pictures with larger file sizes.

faqs.question: Why does the wrong photo print?
faqs.answer:
Check the following:
If your camera supports DPOF, you can pre-select photos so PictureMate knows exactly what to print. See
Printing Camera-Selected DPOF Photos
for more information.
If your camera supports PictBridge or USB DIRECT-PRINT printing, you can connect it to PictureMate and control printing from the camera. See
Printing From a Digital Camera
for details.
For instructions on selecting photos, see
Choosing Photos and Printing
.

faqs.question: Printing is slow. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
It takes a few moments for PictureMate to process your images before printing them. If PictureMate is in a hot or sunny location, move it to a cooler place and try printing again. If you are printing from a computer, make sure your system meets the
System Requirements
.
If you're printing a high-resolution image, you may need more than the minimum requirements listed. You may also need to:
Clear space on your hard drive or run a defragmentation utility.
Close open programs that you're not using.
Increase your system's memory (RAM).
Photos with borders print faster than borderless photos. Also, when you print directly from PictureMate, JPEG photo files print faster than TIFF files. For faster printing, try the following:
Don't print more than 40 pictures at a time.
Turn off special features such as color effects and red-eye reduction.
Before you print from your computer, select
No Correction
(instead of
Auto Correction
) in your print settings.
If PictureMate is connected to a USB hub, disconnect any USB devices that you're not using.

faqs.question: When I try to print to my product in Windows 7, printing is slow or my product stops printing. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Try the following:
Select a lower quality setting in the printer software.
Make sure your system meets the minimum system requirements for your printer.
Close the
Devices and Printers
window before you print.
Clear space on your hard drive or run a defragmentation utility.
Close programs that you're not using.
Increase your system's memory.

faqs.question: I installed a photo cartridge, but an error message says that it is not the initial cartridge. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
For the first cartridge, you must install the photo cartridge that comes in the box with your PictureMate. The label on this cartridge says
Initial Photo Cartridge
. If you purchased additional PictureMate 200 Series Print Packs, use these photo cartridges only as replacements.

The

faqs.question: I replaced an ink cartridge and my product shows that the same ink cartridge is expended. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
If you have just installed a new photo cartridge and you still see a cartridge related error message, the cartridge may be incorrectly installed.
Follow these steps to reinstall the photo cartridge:
Make sure PictureMate is on but not printing.
Open the cartridge door on the back of PictureMate.
Slide the cartridge lever left, to the
Release
position.
Caution
:
Do not try to pull out the cartridge without moving the lever.
Carefully pull out the cartridge.
Warning
:
Keep photo cartridges out of the reach of children and do not drink the ink.
If ink gets on your hands, wash them thoroughly with soap and water. If ink gets in your eyes, flush them thoroughly with water. If discomfort or vision problems continue after flushing, see a doctor immediately.
Slide the cartridge straight into the slot, label side up, until it clicks in place.
Note:
The cartridge won't go in all the way. You need to use the photo cartridge lever to lock it in place.
Slide the lever all the way right to the
Lock
position.
Caution
:
If the cartridge is not inserted correctly, PictureMate will not be able to print. Once the cartridge is installed, do not release or adjust the lever. If you move the lever accidentally, remove the cartridge and reinstall it.
Close the cartridge door all the way.

faqs.question: How do I replace the photo cartridge?
faqs.answer:
See
Replacing the Print Pack
.

faqs.question: How do I know when the photo cartridge needs to be replaced?
faqs.answer:
Your PictureMate will let you know when the photo cartridge is low or expended. See
Checking Print Pack Status
in the User's Guide for more information.

faqs.question: How many photos will I get from my product Print Pack?
faqs.answer:
Actual yields will vary based on images printed, print settings, paper type, frequency of use, and temperature. The number of sheets of photo paper in your PictureMate Print Pack is stated on the Print Pack's box. The photo cartridge in the Print Pack contains enough ink to allow borderless, color printing of about the stated number of sheets.
Get more information
.

faqs.question: Which photo cartridge should I use with my product?
faqs.answer: Use the initial photo cartridge included with PictureMate Dash first. Then use the photo cartridges included with the T5846 or T5845-M Print Packs.

faqs.question: Can the Epson ink cartridges be refilled or can I use third-party ink cartridges without voiding the warranty?
faqs.answer:
Epson does not recommend refilling or using other brands of ink cartridges.  Epson uses a permanent Micro Piezo print head that has allowed Epson to lead the industry in delivering consistent photo image quality by using variable-sized droplets.  Micro Piezo print head can also use a wider variety of inks, which has allowed Epson to introduce such ink breakthroughs as DURABrite® and Epson UltraChrome® inks that offer greatly improved humidity resistance, smudge resistance, and fade resistance.
Using refilled ink cartridges will not void the product's original warranty; however, if these products cause a failure, the repair of that failure will not be covered under warranty.

faqs.question: I brought my product with me to a different country and can't find ink for it. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Some Epson printers and ink cartridges are specific to a regional market and not sold worldwide, although the same printers are sold in the U.S. and Canada. If you have a printer sold in the U.S. or Canada, you may not be able to easily get ink cartridges for it in foreign markets.
Unfortunately, because of customs and tax regulations, the Epson E-Stores in the U.S. and Canada are unable to ship to addresses outside the U.S. and Canada.

faqs.question: How do I clean my product?
faqs.answer:
To keep PictureMate working at its best, you should clean it several times a year.
Turn off PictureMate, unplug the power cable, and disconnect any USB cables or devices.
Remove all paper, then use a soft brush to clean any dust or dirt from the paper feeder and output tray.
Clean the PictureMate exterior with a soft, damp cloth.
Use a soft, dry cloth to clean the PictureMate photo viewer screen. Do not use liquid or chemical cleaners on it.
Caution:
Never use a hard or abrasive brush, or alcohol or thinner for cleaning; they can damage the components and case.
Don't get water on the components and don't spray lubricants or oils inside PictureMate.

faqs.question: My product lid (paper support) snapped off. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Try replacing the lid by inserting the hinges in the brackets.

faqs.question: Why doesn't my product see any photos on the memory card?
faqs.answer:
If your PictureMate Dash is not seeing your photos, check the following:
Make sure you're using a
Compatible Memory Card
.
Make sure only one card is inserted at a time. PictureMate Dash does not read from multiple cards at once.
Make sure your photos are in JPEG or uncompressed TIFF format. If you're using JPEGs, make sure they are non-progressive.  PictureMate Dash can't read progressive-scan JPEG or RAW files.
Make sure the resolution of your photos is between 80 × 80 and 9200 × 9200.

faqs.question: Can my product read multiple memory cards at the same time?
faqs.answer: No. Insert just one card at a time.

faqs.question: I deleted some photos from my memory card and now it isn't working in my camera. What should I do?
faqs.answer: If you use your computer to delete pictures from a memory card, the card may not work correctly with your camera. If this happens, back up the memory card pictures to your computer, then use the camera to format the card. Remember to always delete your camera's pictures using your camera, not your computer.

faqs.question: How do I transfer photos from a memory card to my computer?
faqs.answer:
See
Copying Photos to and From Your Computer
.

faqs.question: Can my product read the images on my memory card that were saved in Adobe Photoshop?
faqs.answer: Yes, but PictureMate cannot read JPEG files that have been opened and saved in Adobe Photoshop using the progressive save option. Files must be saved using the standard option.

faqs.question: I am having problems using a memory card with my product. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Check the following:
Insert only one card at a time.
Make sure you're using a compatible memory card; see
Compatible Memory Cards
.
PictureMate recognizes and can print the first 999 photos on a memory card.
Photos must be JPEG or uncompressed TIFF format and taken with a DCF-compliant digital camera (a camera that complies with the Design rule for Camera File system).
PictureMate can't read progressive-scan JPEG files or RAW files.
If you access the card from your computer and delete files, the card may not work correctly with your camera. Always delete pictures using your camera.
Always format your memory card in your camera.
If you copy files from Adobe Photoshop to a memory card, save them as RGB images using the standard save option (non-progressive). Files saved in the CMYK format may not print with the colors you expect.
Make sure you follow the instructions in the Basics book to install the PictureMate software.
If you're using Windows XP or XP Professional x64 Edition, you may need to install your Windows storage device driver. See your Windows help for more information.

faqs.question: What is the largest supported memory card for my product?
faqs.answer:
See our
Maximum Memory Card Specifications
page for the specifications.

faqs.question: What types of paper can I use with my product?
faqs.answer:
You can use the following:
Size
4 × 6 inches
Paper Types
PictureMate photo paper (included with PictureMate 200 Series Print Pack)
Epson Premium Photo Paper Glossy
Epson Premium Photo Paper Semigloss
Since the quality of any particular brand or type of paper may be changed by the manufacturer at any time, Epson cannot guarantee the quality of any non-Epson brand or type of paper.
Caution:
Don't load plain paper; this may cause damage to PictureMate.

faqs.question: Can I print on plain paper with my product?
faqs.answer: No. If you load plain paper, you may damage PictureMate.

faqs.question: The paper will not feed correctly. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Check the following:
If paper doesn't feed, remove it, separate the sheets slightly, reload it between the edge guides, and make sure the guides aren't too tight.
Make sure the handle is not resting on the paper.
If multiple pages feed at once, remove the paper, separate the sheets, and carefully reload it.
If paper is jammed, remove any sheets behind the jammed paper and press
OK
to eject the jammed paper. Don't pull out jammed paper from the top of PictureMate.
If your paper loads incorrectly or jams frequently:
Use new paper, loaded glossy or whiter side up and separate the sheets slightly.
Make sure you don't load more than 20 sheets.
Make sure your paper is beneath the arrow on the edge guides.
Use only PictureMate Photo Paper, or Epson Premium Photo Paper Glossy or Semigloss. Plain paper may damage your PictureMate.
Store paper flat to prevent curling.

faqs.question: My product sounds as though it is printing, but nothing prints. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Check the following:
PictureMate may be preparing to print.
PictureMate won't operate properly if it's tilted or at an angle. Place it on a flat, stable surface that extends beyond the base in all directions.
Make sure the print head nozzles are not clogged. To clean the print head, see
Improving Print Quality
.
Make sure paper is not jammed and is loaded correctly, and make sure the handle is not resting on the paper.

faqs.question: My printout has lines running through it. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Try the following:
The print head may need cleaning or aligning; see
Improving Print Quality
for instructions.
Make sure the glossy or whiter side of the paper is face-up.
The Print Pack may need replacing; see
Replace the Print Pack
.

faqs.question: My printout is blurry or smeared. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Check the following:
If your paper is damp or curled, load new paper.
Use PictureMate photo paper to ensure proper saturation, absorption of ink, and quality.
Make sure the glossy or whiter side of the paper is face up.
The print head may need cleaning or aligning; see
Improving Print Quality
for instructions.
Remove each photo from the output tray after printing. Let each photo sit for a minute before handling it.

faqs.question: My product is printing blank pages. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
The print head may need cleaning. See
Improving Print Quality
.

faqs.question: My printout is grainy when I print from any application. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Check the following:
Make sure the glossy and whiter side of the paper is face-up. It's usually brighter or whiter.
You may need to increase the image resolution or print in a smaller size; see your software documentation.

faqs.question: The printout is faint or has gaps. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Check the following:
The print head may need cleaning, see
Improving Print Quality
for instructions.
The photo cartridge may be old or ink may be low. See
Replacing the Print Pack
.
Make sure your paper isn't damaged, old, dirty, or loaded facedown. If it is, load new paper with the glossy or whiter side up.

faqs.question: Is there a print test I can run to determine what is causing my print quality problem?
faqs.answer:
Yes. See
Checking the Print Quality Using the Computer
to determine if a problem is being caused by your PictureMate or some other source.

faqs.question: My images saved as CMYK do not look correct. What should I do?
faqs.answer: PictureMate automatically converts RGB images to CMYK. If the image is already CMYK, the color output will not be as expected. Try saving your images as RGB before printing.

faqs.question: My pictures are rotated sideways in the Print Preview screen on my product when I print portrait-oriented photos. Are my photos going to print correctly?
faqs.answer: Yes. If you are printing portrait-oriented photos, they may appear rotated in the confirmation screen, but they will print correctly.

faqs.question: Why do my prints look blotchy?
faqs.answer: The prints may look blotchy before they dry completely. Lay them flat and allow them to dry. Do not stack your photos with the printed sides touching.

faqs.question: Why are the borders or layout incorrect?
faqs.answer:
Check the following:
Check the Layout setting. See
Choosing a Layout
(if printing directly from PictureMate) or
Printing From Your Computer
for instructions.
Try cropping your photo to enlarge and print only a part of it. See
Zooming and Cropping
.
When you print borderless photos, PictureMate automatically expands your images. If too much of your photos are cut off around the edges or if the borders are skewed, you can adjust the amount of expansion. See
Adjusting Borderless Expansion
(if printing directly from PictureMate) or
Printing From Your Computer
(if printing from a computer).
Your photo size may not match the width/height proportions (aspect ratio) of PictureMate photo paper or the layout you're using. Photos may be cropped to fit the paper and layout.
You may have cropped your photo.

faqs.question: The colors in my printed photo are wrong or missing. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
The problem could be due to a software setting or the condition of the PictureMate. Check the following:
If you are printing directly from PictureMate, make sure Color Effect is not set to
Sepia
or
B & W
.
If you are printing from your computer, make sure the Color Option is not set to
Sepia
or
Black & White
.
The print head may need cleaning; see
Improving Print Quality
for instructions.
The photo cartridge may be old or ink may be low; See
Replacing the Print Pack
them.
Turn on the
Enhance
or
P.I.M.
setting, or try manually adjusting the brightness, saturation, or sharpness.
If you copy files from Adobe Photoshop to a memory card, save them as RGB images using the standard save option (non-progressive). Files saved in the CMYK format may not print with the colors you expect.
Colors may change slightly after your print dries. Wait for 24 hours and check your photo again.
Make sure your software is set for color printing.

faqs.question: My prints have too much magenta in them. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Change the
Color Effect
setting to
None
. You can apply the color effect to one photo or all photos currently selected for printing.
Do the following:
Select a photo or photos to print.
Press the
Menu
button.
Press
or
to highlight
Edit
, then press
OK
.
Press
or
to highlight
Color Effect
, then press
OK
.
Press
or
to select
None
, then press
OK
.
At the next screen, select whether to apply the color effect to the current photo or all photos, then press
OK
. You see your photo(s) with the color effect you selected.

faqs.question: How do I uninstall my product software?
faqs.answer:
Follow the instructions below for your computer system.
Note:
Do not turn off or disconnect PictureMate while you are uninstalling the software.
Windows
Click
Start
or
, and select
Programs
or
All Programs
.
Select
Epson
or
Epson Printers
, then select
Epson Printer Software Uninstall
.
Note:
With Windows Vista, click
Continue
, then go to the next step.
In the next window, select your
Epson PictureMate
and click
OK
. Then follow the on-screen instructions.
Restart your computer.
Macintosh
Quit all running applications.
Insert the PictureMate software CD-ROM in your CD-ROM or DVD drive.
Double-click the
OSX
folder. You may have to scroll down to see the folder.
Double click the
Installer
icon. If the Authenticate dialog box appears, enter your password or phrase and click OK.
When the Installer window appears, select
Uninstall
from the pop-up menu at the upper left and click
Uninstall
.
Follow the on-screen instructions to uninstall the PictureMate software.
Restart your Macintosh.
When you are ready to reinstall the PictureMate software, follow the instructions for your operating system in your Basics book.
Note:
Remember that you don't need to reinstall ArcSoft PhotoImpression or your on-screen User's Guide, and you won't see the license agreement.

faqs.question: How can I get the latest my product software?
faqs.answer: You can download the latest software from the Downloads tab.

faqs.question: How can I print wirelessly from a Bluetooth device with my product?
faqs.answer:
See
Printing Wirelessly From a Bluetooth Device
.

faqs.question: Can my product be networked?
faqs.answer:
Yes. You can set up PictureMate as a shared printer. See
Setting Up Network Printing
.

faqs.question: Can I connect my digital camera to my product and print directly from the camera?
faqs.answer:
You can print directly from a digital camera that supports PictBridge or USB DIRECT-PRINT. For more information, see
Printing From a Digital Camera
.

faqs.question: Can I restore my product print settings to their original values?
faqs.answer:
Yes. See
Returning to Default Settings
.

faqs.question: I am having problems installing my product software. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
See
Software Installation Problems
.

faqs.question: Does Epson make drivers for Linux?
faqs.answer:
Linux drivers are available for some products. Visit the links below to see the drivers available for your product, as well as information about using an Epson product with Linux.
Note:
Epson does not provide support for Linux drivers.
Linux drivers for Epson products
Linux FAQs for Epson products
(only available in English)
Linux manuals for Epson products
(only available in English)

faqs.question: I can't find some of my printer's settings in macOS 12 or later. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Make sure you're using the Epson driver for your printer. See our
Adding a Printer in macOS 12 or Later
page for instructions.

faqs.question: How do I add my Epson printer to the Printer list in macOS 12 or later?
faqs.answer:
See our
Adding a Printer in macOS 12 or Later
page for details.

faqs.question: I am unable to connect my product to a wireless network. What should I do?
faqs.answer: The printer does not come with built-in wireless features and does not support a wireless (or Ethernet) connection to a network router. Only a direct wired connection to the computer is supported.

faqs.question: Nothing happens when I try to print. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
If you're printing from your computer, make sure the USB cable is connected securely at both ends and that the cable meets the
System Requirements
.
If you're printing on a network, see
Setting Up Network Printing
for instructions on configuring your PictureMate software for use on a network.

faqs.question: Too many copies are print. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Make sure that the
Copies
option in your software or on PictureMate is set for the number of copies you want to print.

faqs.question: How should I transport my product?
faqs.answer:
See
Taking PictureMate With You
.

faqs.question: Which Epson products support printing from my Sony PlayStation 3?
faqs.answer:
You can print from the Sony Playstation 3 on any of the following Epson printers:
PictureMate Dash
PictureMate Zoom
PictureMate Deluxe
PictureMate Express
PictureMate Pal
PictureMate Snap
PictureMate Flash
Stylus CX3800 / CX3810
Stylus CX4200
Stylus CX4800
Stylus CX5000
Stylus CX6000
Stylus CX7800
Stylus Photo R260
Stylus Photo R340
Stylus Photo R380
Stylus Photo RX580
Please see the

faqs.question: Where can I purchase the optional battery for my product?
faqs.answer: You can purchase the battery from the Epson Store or from a local Epson dealer.

faqs.question: How long does it take to charge the battery?
faqs.answer: It takes approximately 2 hours to fully charge the battery when PictureMate is off. It takes longer if you use PictureMate while it is charging.

faqs.question: My On light is lit, but the viewer screen is blank. Why?
faqs.answer: The screen turns off after 13 minutes if PictureMate is not used. Press any button to turn it back on.

faqs.question: The On light and the photo viewer screen will not turn on. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Try the following:
Press the
On
button again to turn on PictureMate.
Make sure the power cable and AC adapter are securely connected at both ends
Make sure your power outlet works and is not controlled by a wall switch or timer.
If you're using the optional battery, it may not be charged. Connect the AC adapter and plug it into an electrical outlet to charge the battery.
If you're using the optional battery, PictureMate automatically turns off after 15 minutes if it is not being used. Press the
On
button to turn it back on.

faqs.question: My product makes noise after I turn it on or after it has been sitting for a while. What should I do?
faqs.answer: This is normal. It is performing routine maintenance.

faqs.question: Does Epson have a program where I can donate my working electronic equipment?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Epson America, Inc. and
Digitunity
have joined together with the goal of helping those who are facing economic challenges or have a disability to gain access to today's technology. With your donation, you not only help the environment, but you also help change the lives of those who need these products the most.
